PROFESSIONAL WORK · ADVITIIX TECHNOVATE

AI Industrial Inspection & Monitoring

Redesigning mission-critical plant safety monitoring around physical spatial geography—connecting computer vision telemetry, AI confidence scoring, and instantaneous emergency response.

{/* Metadata Grid */}
Role UX/UI & Product Designer
Company Advitiix Technovate

{/* Interactive Floor Map Visualization */}
FIG 1.0 · SPATIAL 2D FLOOR MAP & ACTIVE THERMAL OVERLAY Eliminating mental translation between camera IDs and physical plant geography
{/* ===================================================== 2. PROBLEM STATEMENT ====================================================== */}
// 02 · PROBLEM DISCOVERY

When seconds count, mental translation causes fatal delays

In high-risk manufacturing plants, legacy monitoring tools displayed fire alerts as rows in a tabular database: ID: 4092 · DEV_CAM_24 · TRIGGER_LEVEL_HIGH.

Operators on 12-hour night shifts had to mentally recall where CAM_24 was mounted, cross-check floor blueprints, and decide whether a steam leak or lighting reflection had tripped a false alarm.

Severe Alert Fatigue

High rates of false-positive triggers led operators to silence sirens or delay response until external confirmation arrived.

Zero Immediate Spatial Context

Emergency dispatch requires knowing whether an incident is adjacent to hazardous chemical storage or emergency evacuation routes.

{/* ===================================================== 3. TARGET USERS & OPERATIONAL STAKEHOLDERS ====================================================== */}
// 03 · OPERATIONAL PERSONAS

Designing for High-Stress Control Rooms

OPERATOR 01

Control Room Safety Officer

Monitors 40+ camera feeds simultaneously across 3 monitors. Needs immediate peripheral visual cues and sub-second verification.

OPERATOR 02

On-Floor Emergency Marshal

Receives dispatch notifications on ruggedized mobile tablets. Needs exact door numbers, hazardous material warnings, and fire extinguisher locations.

OPERATOR 03

EHS Compliance Auditor

Reviews historical drill records, false alarm ratios, and camera uptime percentages to fulfill OSHA and insurance compliance audits.

{/* ===================================================== 5 & 6. KEY FEATURES & INTERFACE SOLUTIONS ====================================================== */}
// 05 & 06 · INTERFACE SOLUTIONS

Visual solutions engineered for high clarity

Confidence-Tiered Alert Hierarchy

Rather than treating all alerts with screaming red sirens, we instituted 3 clear confidence tiers: Critical Verified (>85%) triggering audio-visual siren pulses; Advisory (60–84%) requiring operator visual inspection; and System Diagnostics (<60%) logged silently for model re-training.

Split-View Verification Cockpit

Tapping any alert instantly splits the operator display: the left pane shows the 2D architectural blueprint with evacuation vectors, while the right pane streams high-definition thermal video with bounding box telemetry and temperature gradients.

Component System & Frontend Considerations

WebSocket Real-Time Event Dispatch

Engineered alert payload contracts over persistent secure WebSockets with automated fallback polling (500ms intervals) during factory network degradation.

Vector-Based Canvas Coordinate Mapping

Mapped physical plant CAD vectors directly to SVG viewports, allowing facility managers to update camera mounting points via drag-and-drop admin controls without code changes.
